The Chinese philosophy of information innovatively provides a philosophical definition of the concepts of subject and object from the dimension of information activity, while also making specific provisions for the cognitive activities of the subject. The subject's psychology and cognition are an activity of advanced grasping and creation of information. The subject's information activities have five basic levels. Arranged from lower to higher, they are: the subject's in-itself information activities, the subject's intuitive discernment of information, the subject's memory storage of information, the subject's subjective creation of information, and the subject's practice and social realization of information. Higher-level information activities must arise on the basis of lower-level ones. Therefore, the emergence and development of the subject's psychology and cognition necessarily constitute a highly integrated and complex process of information activities.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1884252\", \"pmid\": \"42819459\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13624133\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1884252\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13624133\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13624133?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Digital pharmaka and the crisis of subjectivation: a longitudinal phenomenological study on the educational use of technology in higher education through t…

The subject's psychology and cognition are an activity of advanced grasping and creation of information. The subject's information activities have five basic levels. Arranged from lower to higher, they are: the subject's in-itself information activities, the subject's intuitive discernment of information, the subject's memory storage of information, the subject's subjective creation of information, and the subject's practice and social realization of information. Higher-level information activities must arise on the basis of lower-level ones. Therefore, the emergence and development of the subject's psychology and cognition necessarily constitute a highly integrated and complex process of information activities.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1884252\", \"pmid\": \"42819459\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13624133\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1884252\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13624133\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13624133?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Digital pharmaka and the crisis of subjectivation: a longitudinal phenomenological study on the educational use of technology in higher education through the philosophy of Bernard Stiegler.\", \"abstract\": \"This study investigates the ambivalent effects of digital technologies on the subjectivation processes of university students, drawing on Bernard Stiegler's philosophy of technics and the concept of the pharmakon, technology as both remedy and poison. Using a longitudinal qualitative design grounded in interpretative phenomenological analysis (IPA), the research examines how digital technologies - including smartphones, social media, and AI tools - affect students' attention, memory, desires, and sense of self over an academic semester. Data from three waves of in-depth interviews and reflective journals with twelve undergraduates reveal six interrelated themes: (1) from habitual engagement to cognitive embodiment: the internalization of digital technology; (2) the fragmentation of cognitive focus: the collapse of attention regimes; (3) loss of control and addiction-like engagement: perceived dependence on digital tools; (4) disconnection from meaning: digital acceleration and its impact on memory and meaning-making; (5) Erosion of subjective integrity: identity alienation in digital learning; and (6) reclaiming the Pharmakon: moments of remedial engagement. These findings demonstrate that digital technologies not only influence learning behaviors but also restructure the symbolic, affective, and libidinal foundations of student subjectivity, while also revealing fragile but meaningful counter-tendencies through which students reclaim symbolic production and collective desire. The study extends existing empirical research by integrating lived experience with Stiegler's pharmacological lens, offering critical insights into the psychosocial and existential costs of algorithmic learning environments. It concludes by outlining implications for rethinking educational policy and pedagogy to restore attention, care, and symbolic richness in digitally mediated higher education.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1989076\", \"pmid\": \"42923245\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13687051\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1989076\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13687051\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13687051?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"The Embodied Hijack: when Pleistocene minds meet disembodied artificial intelligence.\", \"abstract\": \"The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into everyday life has intensified a long-standing feature of human cognition: the attribution of agency, intention, and understanding to nonhuman systems. People describe language models, virtual assistants, and autonomous technologies as if these systems know, decide, want, or understand, and they continue to do so even when they know the systems have no inner life. The standard account dismisses this as naïve anthropomorphism, the misfiring of evolved agency-detection systems calibrated in the Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness. We argue that the standard account is incomplete. It explains the immediacy of anthropomorphic response but not its persistence even when users know the system has no mind. Drawing on evolutionary psychology, philosophy of agency, and the active inference framework, we advance the Embodied Hijack hypothesis. Across evolutionary time, fluent communication and contingent responsiveness were produced only by embodied, self-maintaining agents with vulnerability and temporal continuity. Current conversational LLM deployments are the first class of entity to reproduce these signals without the grounding properties - biological self-maintenance, vulnerability, and temporal continuity - that historically produced them. The result is a predictable misalignment: users' inferential systems treat these signals as evidence of agency they were calibrated to indicate, producing systematic misattribution. The Embodied Hijack is not irrationality. It is the optimal predictive response of a Pleistocene-calibrated brain to the rupture of the evolutionary invariant that once tied fluent communication to embodied self-maintenance. The framework yields a unique empirical signature: anthropomorphic response will track the signal profile of a system independently of users' propositional beliefs about what the system is. We close by arguing that the goal is epistemic alignment - bringing how users interpret these systems into correspondence with what these systems actually are - and that this alignment is achieved
